angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 915,680 km at 155.30 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.4392 +/- 0.0125 mas (same row, RUWE 0.94): 155.30 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.3162 +/- 0.023 solar radii from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1794 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract): 915,680 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.9698 +/- 0.0328 solar masses from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1794 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5631 +/- 78 K from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1794 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1794 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1794.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.186, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
